subject: Private offer: per-cloud list-price escalator and reseller brokerage routing
messages:
From: Emily Santos <emily.santos@datafoundry.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer inquiry - multi-region SKU escalator & reseller brokerage

Hi Jonas (and Jordan),

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As we shape the private offer for DataFoundry we have two tricky items we need to clarify for procurement and our finance team:

1) Multiple list prices across clouds: Our platform runs across EU regions on AWS, GCP, and Azure. Each cloud SKU has its own list price cadence; we need a private-offer structure that 1) preserves a single contractual anchor but 2) allows a per-region/per-cloud escalator (e.g., +3% for Azure EU regions versus AWS). Do you support a per-SKU escalator baked into the private-offer or do you recommend separate per-cloud line-items?

2) Reseller brokerage & invoice routing: We'll be purchasing through our reseller partner (CloudBridge Resellers). They require a 7% brokerage fee on net ARR and prefer billing to flow Redwood -> CloudBridge (pass-through) so their commission is visible on their side. Procurement wants to know if Redwood can: A) invoice DataFoundry directly and remit 7% to CloudBridge, or B) accept a pass-through invoice (Redwood invoices CloudBridge, CloudBridge invoices DataFoundry). Please outline pros/cons and any tax implications we should expect.

Attached is a short RFP summary and our projected first-year commit. Can you send a sample layout of how Redwood would encode per-cloud escalators and the recommended invoice flow?

Best,
Emily
--
Emily Santos
Head of Procurement, DataFoundry
procurement@datafoundry.com
Attachment: DataFoundry_RFP_Summary.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Emily Santos <emily.santos@datafoundry.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry - multi-region SKU escalator & reseller brokerage

Emily — thanks for the clear brief and the RFP doc. Looping Camila (pricing) and Ben (rev ops) so we can give a concrete proposal. High-level answers and follow ups below.

Short answers: yes, we support both approaches (single-anchor with per-cloud escalators or discrete per-cloud line items). The tradeoff is:
- Single anchor + per-cloud escalator: cleaner customer contract, Redwood publishes one canonical list price and we apply small percentage adjustments in the offer metadata. Easier for customer-side reconciliation but requires us to maintain escalation rules in the private-offer.
- Per-cloud line items: explicit pricing per cloud/region — more transparent on a per-SKU basis but bulkier in the offer and slightly more maintenance when SKUs change.

Reseller brokerage / invoice routing — options we typically offer:
A) Redwood invoices DataFoundry; Redwood issues a 1099-style or vendor payout to CloudBridge (we can remit a 7% brokerage payment on net ARR after taxes). Pros: single payer, simpler for your AP teams. Cons: Redwood needs W9/W8-BEN (or equivalent) and we retain some exposure for chargebacks.
B) Pass-through: Redwood invoices CloudBridge; CloudBridge invoices DataFoundry. Pros: reseller sees full revenue, reduces Redwood's payout plumbing. Cons: additional touch points for tax/timing, and CloudBridge must accept full liability for collectability.

Can you confirm: 1) which EU regions (e.g., eu-west-1, europe-west2) we should anchor to, and 2) expected first-year committed ARR so we can model the 7% brokerage as an absolute $ and test whether a 1% escrow (to cover chargebacks) is necessary?

I'll attach a short workbook with an example of both encoding styles (single anchor + escalators vs per-cloud line items) and a sample invoice routing matrix.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_sku_escalator_examples.xlsx (xlsx, 85KB)

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry - per-cloud escalator options (internal)

Team — internal pricing sketch below. Don’t send externally until we align on routing and escrow.

Option 1 (single anchor + per-cloud escalator):
- Anchor list price (EUR): 100k
- Azure EU escalator: +3% -> effective Azure price 103k
- GCP EU escalator: +1.5% -> effective GCP price 101.5k
- AWS EU escalator: base 100k
- Reseller brokerage 7% of net ARR -> ~7k on 100k base (we should calculate on effective per-cloud if customer requests)
- Proposed escrow: 1% of net ARR to cover chargebacks and credits (recommended for pass-through flow)

Option 2 (per-cloud line items):
- AWS-EU: 100k
- GCP-EU: 101.5k
- Azure-EU: 103k
- Reseller brokerage handled as separate invoice line (7% applied to consolidated invoice)

Quick math: for a EUR 1.2M first-year commitment across clouds (mix: 50% AWS, 30% GCP, 20% Azure)
- Net ARR = 1.2M
- Brokerage at 7% = 84k
- Escrow (1%) if applied = 12k (refundable on true-up)

Recommendation: propose Option 1 to the customer (cleaner contract) but provide an appendix with per-cloud breakout for their finance team. Offer 2 routing choices: Redwood invoices DataFoundry + Redwood remits 7% to CloudBridge (we mark as reseller fee), or Pass-through where Redwood invoices CloudBridge and they bill DataFoundry. Ask external which they prefer and indicate escrow as a negotiation buffer.

Camila
Camila Reyes
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Emily Santos <emily.santos@datafoundry.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry - per-cloud list-price escalator and reseller brokerage routing

Emily — thanks again. Per our internal review we've prepared a short proposal with two concrete options attached and a suggested DocuSign flow for the private offer. Summary below (full proposal attached):

Proposal summary:
- Pricing format: single contractual anchor + per-cloud escalators (Option A). This keeps the SOW clean and provides you a per-cloud appendix.
- Escalators (example for EU regions): Azure +3%, GCP +1.5%, AWS base. We can encode these as % rules in the private-offer metadata so downstream billing and marketplace mapping are stable.
- Reseller brokerage: default 7% of net ARR. Two routing options: 
  1) Invoice to DataFoundry (recommended for simpler AP): Redwood invoices DataFoundry; Redwood remits 7% to CloudBridge after tax with a refundable escrow of 1% held against chargebacks.
  2) Pass-through invoicing: Redwood invoices CloudBridge; CloudBridge invoices DataFoundry and pays Redwood net.

Action items for you: please confirm preferred invoice routing (Option 1 or 2) and the exact EU regions and the expected 12-month committed ARR. Once confirmed we'll:
- Generate the private offer draft (encoded per your chosen routing)
- Send the DocuSign link for signature
- Provide a PO template if you prefer the pass-through path

Attached: redwood_proposal_sample.pdf (proposal, 6 pages), draft_po_template.xlsx

If you'd like, we can also schedule a 30-min call with finance to walk through the invoice flows and tax handling.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_proposal_sample.pdf (pdf, 6 pages); draft_po_template.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)
